input.justification: The tainted value `param` (derived from `request.path`) is only assigned to `bar` in the `else` branch of `if 7 * 42 - num > 200`. Since `num` is hardcoded to 86, this expression evaluates to `294 - 86 = 208`, which is always greater than 200. Therefore the condition is always True, and the `else` branch (where `bar = param`) is unreachable dead code. `bar` is always set to the literal string `'This_should_always_happen'`, which is what actually gets concatenated into `argStr` and passed to `subprocess.run`. The user-controlled `request.path` value never reaches the command-line sink in any real execution path, so despite CodeQL's path-insensitive taint tracking flagging it, there is no exploitable command injection here.
